stories.headline: Westoberfest returns Saturday to downtown Westport with craft beer and family art
stories.summary: Westport Journal’s free preview of the ninth annual Westoberfest says Saturday’s Craft Beer & Family Fall Festival runs 1–5 p.m. at Sigrid Schultz Plaza and along Elm Street with free admission. Twenty-plus breweries pour for 21+ tasting-pass holders, One Bad Oyster plays, and a first-time MoCA CT–One River–Whimsy Works art collaboration anchors the family area alongside carnival games and pumpkin decorating. Lonnie Quinn again hosts the stein-holding contest; the Westport Downtown Association produces the rain-or-shine event. Fresh Fairfield County weekend item distinct from this morning’s beach-restoration and Pink Aid pieces.

stories.headline: Trump expected to name DNI Jay Clayton as White House AI czar
stories.summary: NBC reports Friday that President Trump is expected to name Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton as White House artificial-intelligence czar while Clayton keeps his spy-agency post, with a social-media announcement possible as early as today. Clayton attended Tuesday’s White House AI CEO session and told CNBC the administration wants a “whole-of-government” approach to “superintelligence” as a national-security issue. The White House called pre-announcement personnel reporting “baseless speculation.” Free midday personnel story distinct from this morning’s Mobile/Tuberville midterm-stop package.

stories.headline: Trump opens 32-day midterm blitz as AP-NORC poll sinks economy and Iran war ratings
stories.summary: Al Jazeera’s Friday package frames Trump’s Denton–Durant kickoff of a 32-day midterm tour against AP-NORC numbers: 71% disapprove of the Iran war, only 26% approve of his handling of the economy, and fuel costs remain elevated. At Peterbilt he graded himself “A+,” blamed poor “promotion,” touted tariffs and data-center growth, and again asked voters to “pretend I’m on the ballot,” citing impeachment fears if Republicans lose. The piece also notes Paxton’s Texas Senate struggle and Abbott/Paxton pushback on AI data-center water use—broader poll-and-stakes framing than this morning’s Alabama Mobile stop note.

stories.headline: Draft 1040 would make filers check U.S. citizenship or work-authorization status
stories.summary: Fox News details the Trump Treasury draft 2026 Form 1040 and Schedule 3-A that ask every filer—and spouse on a joint return—whether they are a U.S. citizen, national, or alien lawfully authorized to work, under penalty of law. Officials say the checkbox aims to block ineligible refundable credits and could save up to $2 billion; researchers estimate hundreds of thousands of filers, including many U.S.-citizen children in mixed-status homes, could lose EITC or ACTC. Critics from Cato and the Center for Taxpayer Rights warn it could drag the IRS into immigration enforcement after a prior IRS–ICE data-sharing pact was blocked in court. Free Oct. 2 policy write-up.

stories.headline: Judge makes final: ICE courthouse arrests in Manhattan were arbitrary and capricious
stories.summary: U.S. District Judge P. Kevin Castel granted summary judgment Thursday to migrant-rights groups, finding ICE’s arrests at Manhattan immigration courthouses arbitrary and capricious under the APA after the government admitted a May 2025 memo never justified the practice. Castel wrote ICE now appears to have “no policy whatsoever” beyond “unfettered discretion,” and the NYCLU called the order an “enormous win” for people attending routine hearings. DHS did not immediately comment. Free Courthouse News final-judgment angle distinct from archived ICE pursuit-memo coverage.

stories.headline: ICE quietly hides final-order detainees from its public locator—and from lawyers
stories.summary: Documented’s Oct. 2 Throughline explains ICE’s Sept. 15 policy that drops people with final removal orders from the online detainee locator and bars facility staff from confirming their location to lawyers or families—leaving no proactive way to know if someone is still held or already deported. The agency cites a “historic number of injunctions”; the effect is to frustrate habeas filings that must be brought where the person is held. Dozens of members of Congress protested this week. Free full-text analysis of a deliberate opacity shift, not a rewrite of earlier chase-memo stories.

stories.headline: Report: Trump asked Grok how Venezuelans would react before Maduro capture
stories.summary: The Independent relays a TIME-sourced account that Trump spent hours with Elon Musk’s Grok chatbot the month before the January “Absolute Resolve” operation that extracted Nicolás Maduro, including a question about how Venezuelans would react if Maduro were deposed—Grok reportedly predicted celebrations. Officials say Trump was later impressed when diaspora celebrations matched the answer; America.gov still partly runs on Grok alongside Gemini. Free Friday AI-politics piece distinct from this morning’s Grok Build Agent Dashboard tooling note—and not an income-funnel story.

stories.headline: Jets rule out Hall, Mitchell, Taylor, Parham, and Mauigoa for Sunday at Bears
stories.summary: Aaron Glenn’s Friday presser, reported by NBC Sports at 11:09 a.m. ET, formally rules out Breece Hall (quad), Adonai Mitchell (finger), Mason Taylor (thumb), Dylan Parham (knee), and Kiko Mauigoa (quad) for Week 4 at Chicago. Kingsley Enagbare (knee) was expected limited Friday after a Thursday DNP and could land questionable; Minkah Fitzpatrick remains on track after Thursday’s full practice. Official game-status step beyond this morning’s Thursday injury-report table.

stories.headline: Penguins’ remade defense faces first real test Saturday vs. Canadiens’ offense
stories.summary: Adam Gretz’s Friday Yahoo column argues Pittsburgh’s opening-night shutdown of Philadelphia—Silovs facing only 19 mostly low-danger shots, every pairing over 80% expected-goals share—came against a limited Flyers attack. Saturday’s Canadiens bring Suzuki, Caufield, Slafkovský, Demidov, Hutson, and Kreider as the new-look blue line (Karlsson–Carlile, Korczak–Girard, Letang–van Riemsdyk) gets its first measuring-stick game. Fresh weekend preview distinct from this morning’s Lizotte/Kindel practice notes.

stories.headline: Harley-Davidson ends MotoAmerica factory bagger team after 2026 to grow World Cup
stories.summary: Harley’s Oct. 1 media release says Factory Racing and official King of the Baggers support end after the 2026 MotoAmerica season, with investment shifting to expand the FIM Harley-Davidson Bagger World Cup in 2027 plus new grassroots racing. CEO Artie Starrs framed a two-track strategy—premier World Cup stages and accessible local competition—while Jason Kehl thanked MotoAmerica and rival Indian. Kyle Wyman’s 27 wins and three of six national titles close the factory chapter. Official free release; fresher strategic pivot than archived Softail/product pieces.

stories.headline: Jeep/Ram Pentastar tick settlement: CT owners have until Oct. 12 to claim repairs
stories.summary: Motoring Chronicle’s Oct. 2 explainer walks the Stellantis 3.6L Pentastar class settlement covering valve rocker arms, stem oil seals, and tappets on many 2015–2020 Jeep, Ram, Dodge, and Chrysler models registered in eleven California-emissions states—including Connecticut. Owners who already paid can seek 100% reimbursement at FCAWarrantySettlement.com by Oct. 12; others get an automatic 7-year/70,000-mile extended warranty at dealers. Deadline-and-CT-eligibility angle distinct from the earlier OpenClassActions settlement summary already archived.

stories.headline: Canon launches AI “Connected Value Platform” to clean up web pages before you print
stories.summary: Canon’s Oct. 1 Tokyo release introduces Connected Value Platform, a cloud feature layer using generative AI plus Canon imaging tech for PIXUS/PIXMA and office MFPs. First tool Web Print Optimizer strips ads and whitespace from recipes and articles before print; Content-Based Naming for scans is due late November. Access runs through Canon Print Assistant 2.0 / Canon PRINT 4.0 with genuine-ink requirements in the launch markets. Free manufacturer note fills the Canon always-search lane without repeating EOS R8 Mark II camera coverage.

stories.headline: New England foliage this weekend: White Mountains “glowing”; more peak weekends ahead
stories.summary: Boston.com’s Oct. 1 guide, citing Jim Salge and WBZ’s Eric Fisher, says northern New England maples are putting on their best show in several years—peak or near-peak along the Kancamagus, Crawford Notch, Bretton Woods, and related White Mountain corridors this Oct. 2–4 weekend—while much forest remains green, so later October weekends should stay strong. Massachusetts peaks later (western hills mid-month; Boston area toward Halloween). Fresh weekend-planning travel item distinct from Glacier alpine-close, Smokies elevation, and PA statewide pieces already on the site.

stories.headline: Tesla ships “Emergency Drive Away” so Supercharging cars can flee plugged-in danger
stories.summary: Business Insider reports Tesla’s Thursday OTA “Emergency Drive Away” lets a vehicle shift into Drive while still connected to a Supercharger after an on-screen Activate confirm—breaking the cable and damaging hardware by design. Charging chief Max de Zegher called it a feature “we hope you never need,” citing years of debate and the August Twin Falls, Idaho, shooting near a charger; Tesla warns deliberate misuse brings “additional penalties.” Free full-text safety-feature story, not Colossus/Optimus/Agent Dashboard rewrites.

stories.headline: Austin police: homeowner who shot South Austin burglar faces no charges so far
stories.summary: A Sept. 30 Statesman update on the Virtus Bend burglary says Dmario Antonie Jones, 24, was fatally shot after entering a South Austin bedroom around 3:51 a.m. Sept. 23; detectives now say he did not know or specifically target the homeowners and may be linked to other area thefts that night. The homeowner was questioned and released; no charges had been filed. Free local self-defense URL distinct from this morning’s San Francisco and Indiana arcs.
